passages.text: These are the words of Agur son of Jakeh—the burden that this man declared to Ithiel: “I am weary, O God, and worn out.
passages.sermon:
Agur is the son of Jakeh.
Agur speaks these words.
Agur gives a message.
Agur speaks to Ithiel.
Agur says, "I am weary, O God."
Agur says, "I am worn out."
passages.original: דִּבְרֵ֤י׀ אָג֥וּר בִּן־ יָקֶ֗ה הַמַּ֫שָּׂ֥א נְאֻ֣ם הַ֭גֶּבֶר לְאִֽיתִיאֵ֑ל לְאִ֖יתִיאֵ֣ל וְאֻכָֽל׃

passages.text: Surely I am the most ignorant of men, and I lack the understanding of a man.
passages.sermon:
Agur son of Jakeh speaks these words.
Agur says he is ignorant.
Agur says he is more ignorant than other men.
Agur says he does not have human understanding.
passages.original: כִּ֤י בַ֣עַר אָנֹכִ֣י מֵאִ֑ישׁ וְלֹֽא־ בִינַ֖ת אָדָ֣ם לִֽי׃

passages.text: I have not learned wisdom, and I have no knowledge of the Holy One.
passages.sermon:
Agur son of Jakeh speaks.
Agur says he has not learned wisdom.
Agur says he does not know the Holy One.
Agur admits he lacks knowledge about God.
passages.original: וְלֹֽא־ לָמַ֥דְתִּי חָכְמָ֑ה וְדַ֖עַת קְדֹשִׁ֣ים אֵדָֽע׃

passages.text: Who has ascended to heaven and come down? Who has gathered the wind in His hands? Who has bound up the waters in His cloak? Who has established all the ends of the earth? What is His name, and what is the name of His Son— surely you know!
passages.sermon:
God is the one who has power over all creation.
God has gone up to heaven.
God has come down from heaven.
God has gathered the wind in His hands.
God has wrapped up the waters in His cloak.
God has set all the ends of the earth in place.
God has a name.
God has a Son.
You surely know who He is.
passages.original: מִ֤י עָלָֽה־ שָׁמַ֨יִם׀ וַיֵּרַ֡ד מִ֤י אָֽסַף־ ר֨וּחַ׀ בְּחָפְנָ֡יו מִ֤י צָֽרַר־ מַ֨יִם׀ בַּשִּׂמְלָ֗ה מִ֭י הֵקִ֣ים כָּל־ אַפְסֵי־ אָ֑רֶץ מַה־ שְּׁמ֥וֹ וּמַֽה־ שֶּׁם־ בְּ֝נ֗וֹ כִּ֣י תֵדָֽע׃

passages.text: Every word of God is flawless; He is a shield to those who take refuge in Him.
passages.sermon:
God speaks words.
God’s words are flawless.
God protects people.
He shields everyone who takes refuge in Him.
passages.original: כָּל־ אִמְרַ֣ת אֱל֣וֹהַּ צְרוּפָ֑ה מָגֵ֥ן ה֝֗וּא לַֽחֹסִ֥ים בּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Do not add to His words, lest He rebuke you and prove you a liar.
passages.sermon:
God speaks true words.
Do not add to God's words.
If you add to His words, God may rebuke you.
God may show that you are a liar.
passages.original: אַל־ תּ֥וֹסְףְּ עַל־ דְּבָרָ֑יו פֶּן־ יוֹכִ֖יחַ בְּךָ֣ וְנִכְזָֽבְתָּ׃פ

passages.text: Two things I ask of You— do not refuse me before I die: Keep falsehood and deceitful words far from me. Give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with the bread that is my portion.
passages.sermon:
I speak to God.
I ask God for two things.
I ask God to give me these things before I die.
I ask God to keep lies far from me.
I ask God to keep deceitful words away from me.
I ask God not to give me poverty.
I ask God not to give me riches.
I ask God to give me only the bread I need.
I ask God to give me just enough for each day.
passages.original: שְׁ֭תַּיִם שָׁאַ֣לְתִּי מֵאִתָּ֑ךְ אַל־ תִּמְנַ֥ע מִ֝מֶּ֗נִּי בְּטֶ֣רֶם אָמֽוּת׃ שָׁ֤וְא׀ וּֽדְבַר־ כָּזָ֡ב הַרְחֵ֬ק מִמֶּ֗נִּי רֵ֣אשׁ וָ֭עֹשֶׁר אַל־ תִּֽתֶּן־ לִ֑י הַ֝טְרִיפֵ֗נִי לֶ֣חֶם חֻקִּֽי׃

passages.text: Otherwise, I may have too much and deny You, saying, ‘Who is the LORD?’ Or I may become poor and steal, profaning the name of my God.
passages.sermon:
The speaker prays to God.
He asks God to protect him from two dangers.
First, he fears having too much.
If he has too much, he may deny God.
He may say, “Who is the LORD?”
Second, he fears becoming poor.
If he becomes poor, he may steal.
If he steals, he will dishonor the name of his God.
passages.original: פֶּ֥ן אֶשְׂבַּ֨ע׀ וְכִחַשְׁתִּי֮ וְאָמַ֗רְתִּי מִ֥י יְה֫וָ֥ה וּפֶֽן־ אִוָּרֵ֥שׁ וְגָנַ֑בְתִּי וְ֝תָפַ֗שְׂתִּי שֵׁ֣ם אֱלֹהָֽי׃פ

passages.text: Do not slander a servant to his master, or he will curse you, and you will bear the guilt.
passages.sermon: Do not speak badly about a servant to his master.\r\nIf you do, the servant may curse you.\r\nYou will be guilty if this happens.
passages.original: אַל־ תַּלְשֵׁ֣ן עֶ֭בֶד אֶל־ אֲדֹנוֹ פֶּֽן־ יְקַלֶּלְךָ֥ וְאָשָֽׁמְתָּ׃

passages.text: There is a generation of those who curse their fathers and do not bless their mothers.
passages.sermon:
This passage describes a certain kind of people.
These people belong to a generation.
They curse their fathers.
They do not bless their mothers.
passages.original: דּ֭וֹר אָבִ֣יו יְקַלֵּ֑ל וְאֶת־ אִ֝מּ֗וֹ לֹ֣א יְבָרֵֽךְ׃

passages.text: There is a generation of those who are pure in their own eyes and yet unwashed of their filth.
passages.sermon:
Some people belong to a certain generation.
This generation thinks they are pure.
They see themselves as clean and good.
But they are not truly clean.
They have not washed away their own filth.
They remain dirty, even though they believe they are pure.
passages.original: דּ֭וֹר טָה֣וֹר בְּעֵינָ֑יו וּ֝מִצֹּאָת֗וֹ לֹ֣א רֻחָֽץ׃

passages.text: There is a generation—how haughty are their eyes and pretentious are their glances— there is a generation whose teeth are swords and whose jaws are knives, devouring the oppressed from the earth and the needy from among men.
passages.sermon:
There is a generation.
This generation looks with pride.
Their eyes are haughty.
Their glances are arrogant.
This generation has sharp teeth.
Their teeth are like swords.
Their jaws are like knives.
They devour the poor from the earth.
They consume the needy from among people.
passages.original: דּ֭וֹר מָה־ רָמ֣וּ עֵינָ֑יו וְ֝עַפְעַפָּ֗יו יִנָּשֵֽׂאוּ׃ דּ֤וֹר׀ חֲרָב֣וֹת שִׁנָּיו֮ וּֽמַאֲכָל֪וֹת מְֽתַלְּעֹ֫תָ֥יו לֶאֱכֹ֣ל עֲנִיִּ֣ים מֵאֶ֑רֶץ וְ֝אֶבְיוֹנִ֗ים מֵאָדָֽם׃פ

passages.text: The leech has two daughters: Give and Give. There are three things that are never satisfied, four that never say, ‘Enough!’: Sheol, the barren womb, land never satisfied with water, and fire that never says, ‘Enough!’
passages.sermon:
The leech is a creature that feeds on the blood of others.
The leech has two daughters.
These daughters always cry out, "Give! Give!"
There are three things that are never satisfied.
There are four things that never say, "Enough!"
The grave never has enough.
A barren womb never feels satisfied.
The land is never filled with water.
Fire never says, "Enough!"
passages.original: לַֽעֲלוּקָ֨ה׀ שְׁתֵּ֥י בָנוֹת֮ הַ֤ב׀ הַ֥ב שָׁל֣וֹשׁ הֵ֭נָּה לֹ֣א תִשְׂבַּ֑עְנָה אַ֝רְבַּ֗ע לֹא־ אָ֥מְרוּ הֽוֹן׃ שְׁאוֹל֮ וְעֹ֪צֶ֫ר רָ֥חַם אֶ֭רֶץ לֹא־ שָׂ֣בְעָה מַּ֑יִם וְ֝אֵ֗שׁ לֹא־ אָ֥מְרָה הֽוֹן׃

passages.text: As for the eye that mocks a father and scorns obedience to a mother, may the ravens of the valley pluck it out and young vultures devour it.
passages.sermon:
This passage warns about disrespecting parents.
A person may mock his father.
He may scorn obedience to his mother.
Such a person shows pride and contempt.
Ravens of the valley will pluck out his eye.
Young vultures will eat it.
This is a warning of severe consequences for dishonoring parents.
passages.original: עַ֤יִן׀ תִּֽלְעַ֣ג לְאָב֮ וְתָב֪וּז לִֽיקֲּהַ֫ת־ אֵ֥ם יִקְּר֥וּהָ עֹרְבֵי־ נַ֑חַל וְֽיֹאכְל֥וּהָ בְנֵי־ נָֽשֶׁר׃פ

passages.text: There are three things too wonderful for me, four that I cannot understand: the way of an eagle in the sky, the way of a snake on a rock, the way of a ship at sea, and the way of a man with a maiden.
passages.sermon:
The writer speaks about things that are too wonderful for him to understand.
He says there are three things that amaze him.
He says there are four things he cannot understand.
The first is the way of an eagle in the sky.
The second is the way of a snake on a rock.
The third is the way of a ship in the heart of the sea.
The fourth is the way of a man with a young woman.
passages.original: שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה הֵ֭מָּה נִפְלְא֣וּ מִמֶּ֑נִּי וְאַרְבָּע לֹ֣א יְדַעְתִּֽים׃ דֶּ֤רֶךְ הַנֶּ֨שֶׁר׀ בַּשָּׁמַיִם֮ דֶּ֥רֶךְ נָחָ֗שׁ עֲלֵ֫י צ֥וּר דֶּֽרֶךְ־ אֳנִיָּ֥ה בְלֶב־ יָ֑ם וְדֶ֖רֶךְ גֶּ֣בֶר בְּעַלְמָֽה׃

passages.text: This is the way of an adulteress: She eats and wipes her mouth and says, ‘I have done nothing wrong.’
passages.sermon:
An adulteress acts in a certain way.
She eats.
She wipes her mouth.
She says, “I have done nothing wrong.”
passages.original: כֵּ֤ן׀ דֶּ֥רֶךְ אִשָּׁ֗ה מְנָ֫אָ֥פֶת אָ֭כְלָה וּמָ֣חֲתָה פִ֑יהָ וְ֝אָמְרָ֗ה לֹֽא־ פָעַ֥לְתִּי אָֽוֶן׃פ

passages.text: Under three things the earth trembles, under four it cannot bear up: a servant who becomes king, a fool who is filled with food, an unloved woman who marries, and a maidservant who supplants her mistress.
passages.sermon:
The earth trembles under three things.
The earth cannot bear up under four things.
A servant becomes king.
A fool is filled with food.
An unloved woman gets married.
A maidservant takes her mistress’s place.
passages.original: תַּ֣חַת שָׁ֭לוֹשׁ רָ֣גְזָה אֶ֑רֶץ וְתַ֥חַת אַ֝רְבַּ֗ע לֹא־ תוּכַ֥ל שְׂאֵֽת׃ תַּֽחַת־ עֶ֭בֶד כִּ֣י יִמְל֑וֹךְ וְ֝נָבָ֗ל כִּ֣י יִֽשְׂבַּֽע־ לָֽחֶם׃ תַּ֣חַת שְׂ֭נוּאָה כִּ֣י תִבָּעֵ֑ל וְ֝שִׁפְחָ֗ה כִּֽי־ תִירַ֥שׁ גְּבִרְתָּֽהּ׃פ

passages.text: Four things on earth are small, yet they are exceedingly wise: The ants are creatures of little strength, yet they store up their food in the summer; the rock badgers are creatures of little power, yet they make their homes in the rocks; the locusts have no king, yet they all advance in formation; and the lizard can be caught in one’s hands, yet it is found in the palaces of kings.
passages.sermon:
There are four small things on earth.
These four things are very wise.
Ants are not strong.
Ants prepare their food in the summer.
Rock badgers are not powerful.
Rock badgers make their homes in the rocks.
Locusts have no king.
Locusts all move forward together in order.
A lizard can be caught with the hands.
A lizard is found in the palaces of kings.
passages.original: אַרְבָּ֣עָה הֵ֭ם קְטַנֵּי־ אָ֑רֶץ וְ֝הֵ֗מָּה חֲכָמִ֥ים מְחֻכָּמִֽים׃ הַ֭נְּמָלִים עַ֣ם לֹא־ עָ֑ז וַיָּכִ֖ינוּ בַקַּ֣יִץ לַחְמָֽם׃ שְׁ֭פַנִּים עַ֣ם לֹא־ עָצ֑וּם וַיָּשִׂ֖ימוּ בַסֶּ֣לַע בֵּיתָֽם׃ מֶ֭לֶךְ אֵ֣ין לָאַרְבֶּ֑ה וַיֵּצֵ֖א חֹצֵ֣ץ כֻּלּֽוֹ׃ שְׂ֭מָמִית בְּיָדַ֣יִם תְּתַפֵּ֑שׂ וְ֝הִ֗יא בְּהֵ֣יכְלֵי מֶֽלֶךְ׃פ

passages.text: There are three things that are stately in their stride, and four that are impressive in their walk: a lion, mighty among beasts, refusing to retreat before anything; a strutting rooster; a he-goat; and a king with his army around him.
passages.sermon:
There are three things that walk with stately steps.
There are four things that walk in an impressive way.
The lion is mighty among the animals.
The lion does not turn back from anything.
The strutting rooster walks with pride.
The he-goat walks with confidence.
The king walks with his army around him.
The king walks with authority and strength.
passages.original: שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה הֵ֭מָּה מֵיטִ֣יבֵי צָ֑עַד וְ֝אַרְבָּעָ֗ה מֵיטִ֥בֵי לָֽכֶת׃ לַ֭יִשׁ גִּבּ֣וֹר בַּבְּהֵמָ֑ה וְלֹא־ יָ֝שׁ֗וּב מִפְּנֵי־ כֹֽל׃ זַרְזִ֣יר מָתְנַ֣יִם אוֹ־ תָ֑יִשׁ וּ֝מֶ֗לֶךְ אַלְק֥וּם עִמּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: If you have foolishly exalted yourself or if you have plotted evil, put your hand over your mouth.
passages.sermon:
This passage gives a warning about pride and evil plans.

If you act foolishly and make yourself proud, stop.

If you plan to do evil, stop.

Cover your mouth with your hand.

Do not speak or act on your pride or evil plans.
passages.original: אִם־ נָבַ֥לְתָּ בְהִתְנַשֵּׂ֑א וְאִם־ זַ֝מּ֗וֹתָ יָ֣ד לְפֶֽה׃

passages.text: For as the churning of milk yields butter, and the twisting of the nose draws blood, so the stirring of anger brings forth strife.”
passages.sermon: Churning milk makes butter.\r\nTwisting a nose makes blood come out.\r\nStirring up anger makes strife.
passages.original: כִּ֤י מִ֪יץ חָלָ֡ב י֘וֹצִ֤יא חֶמְאָ֗ה וּֽמִיץ־ אַ֭ף י֣וֹצִיא דָ֑ם וּמִ֥יץ אַ֝פַּ֗יִם י֣וֹצִיא רִֽיב׃פ
